Next: Sun, Nov 29 at Chargers, 4:05 PM

storylines: Winnipeg (12–9–4) has won three straight road games; Boston beat the Jets 4–3 in overtime on Oct. 2.
The Bruins come off three days between games, which Marco Sturm said he doesn't like: "we play better when we play a lot of games in a short time."
James Hagens returned to practice Tuesday in a non-contact jersey but has no return date.
bruins.edge: Boston on paper: it allows 2.65 goals a game, fourth in the NHL, to Winnipeg's 3.32, though the Jets' power play (23.3%) is ahead of Boston's (19.4%).

storylines: Boston (3–0 in NBA Cup play) hosts Atlanta (2–1), and the winner finishes atop East Group C.
Tatum is coming off 41 points, his most since his Achilles injury, and Paul George just reached 2,500 career threes.
Mitchell Robinson (illness) has missed three straight games.
celtics.edge: Close on paper: Boston is 12–6 and Atlanta 11–6, with the Celtics at home.

storylines: New England (5–5, eighth in the AFC) comes off its bye at 1–9 Los Angeles, in a game moved from Sunday night to 4:05 p.m. on CBS.
Tommy DeVito starts for the injured Drake Maye, and the Patriots are carrying only two healthy quarterbacks, with rookie Behren Morton the backup.
A.J. Brown (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple weeks, while Romeo Doubs and Alijah Vera-Tucker are eligible to return.
patriots.edge: New England on paper against a 1–9 team, though it is without Maye and A.J. Brown and managed 151 yards in Munich.

results.headline: Tatum's 41 snaps Celtics' four-game skid
results.takeaway: Jayson Tatum scored 41, 28 in the first half, as Boston led 80–49 at the break and held off a Washington rally that got within 117–112. The win ends a four-game skid and keeps the Celtics 3–0 in NBA Cup play.

videos.title: Celtics at Wizards: full game highlights

sections.label: 1st quarter
sections.text: Neemias Queta scored 13 points before Anthony Davis had any, and Tatum had 15 points and five assists in the quarter. Boston led 21–9 with 5:52 left and 34–28 after one.

sections.label: 2nd quarter
sections.text: The Celtics opened the quarter on a 14–3 run, capped by Payton Pritchard's three for a 48–31 lead at 9:02. A later 11–0 run with three Tatum threes made it 70–38 with 2:19 left; Boston made 10 threes in a 46-point quarter, and Tatum had 28 at the half.

sections.label: 3rd quarter
sections.text: Washington outscored Boston 40–24 and cut it to 94–81 on Bilal Coulibaly's dunk with 3:20 left. Paul George answered with a step-back three and Pritchard scored the next five for a 102–81 lead, before two Coulibaly threes and Trae Young free throws made it a 15-point game.

sections.label: 4th quarter
sections.text: Davis and AJ Dybantsa led a Wizards push, and Dybantsa's bank shot made it 117–112 with 3:19 left. Tatum's layup made it 119–112, then Baylor Scheierman, scoreless until then, scored Boston's next eight: a three at 2:31, two free throws and a 30-footer for 127–114 with 1:16 left.

performers.name: Jayson Tatum
performers.note: His most points since returning from his Achilles injury, and his 31st career 40-point game; he set up Scheierman's late threes too.

performers.name: Paul George
performers.note: Became the eighth player in NBA history to reach 2,500 career threes and was +34.

performers.name: Neemias Queta
performers.note: A season high, including 13 points in the first quarter before Anthony Davis scored.

results.oppLine: Anthony Davis had 33 points and 13 rebounds; Kyshawn George added 24, AJ Dybantsa 20 points, 11 rebounds and 7 assists, and Trae Young 17 points and 12 assists.

celtics.headline: Skid over; Cup group decided Friday
celtics.summary: The win ended Boston's four-game losing streak and kept the Celtics unbeaten in NBA Cup play at 3–0. They host Atlanta (2–1) on Friday, with the winner finishing atop the group.

celtics.headline: George reaches 2,500 career threes
celtics.summary: Paul George became the eighth player in NBA history to make 2,500 3-pointers, on a 6-of-9 night from deep with 28 points and nine assists. Neemias Queta added a season-high 21 on 9-of-11 shooting.

celtics.headline: Tatum's biggest night since the Achilles
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum's 41 points were his most since 46 against Cleveland on Feb. 28, 2025, and his 31st career 40-point game. "We had a tough last week, for various reasons," he said. "We can't change what happened; we can only focus on today."

celtics.headline: Mazzulla ties Phil Jackson to 250 wins
celtics.summary: Joe Mazzulla reached 250 wins in his 346th game, tying Phil Jackson as the second-fastest coach to get there. Only Steve Kerr (302 games) did it faster.

celtics.headline: Robinson misses a third straight game
celtics.summary: Mitchell Robinson (illness) was out again Tuesday at Washington, his third straight missed game. Dillon Mitchell and Amari Williams were assigned to the G League.

celtics.headline: Scheierman's late eight
celtics.summary: Baylor Scheierman, scoreless for the first 45 and a half minutes, scored eight straight Celtics points in 1:15 after Washington cut a 34-point lead to seven. Boston was playing its third game in four nights.

celtics.headline: Dybantsa's first game against his hometown team
celtics.summary: Brockton native AJ Dybantsa had 20 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists in his first career game against the Celtics.

celtics.headline: Tatum passes Bill Russell
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum's 27 points against the Warriors moved him to 14,528 career points, past Bill Russell (14,522) for eighth on the Celtics' all-time scoring list. Sam Jones is seventh at 15,411.

celtics.headline: Mazzulla on Conley: 'he gave us a chance to win'
celtics.summary: Mike Conley scored 19 off the bench, going 4-for-4 from three. "Tonight's the reason why you have a guy like that on your roster," Joe Mazzulla said.

bruins.headline: Hagens back at practice
bruins.summary: James Hagens, out since a cross-check against Pittsburgh on Nov. 5, practiced Tuesday in a non-contact jersey. "This is the next block," Marco Sturm said; neither he nor Hagens gave a return date. Hagens has 12 points in 17 games.

bruins.headline: NESN's Garden Party returns Thanksgiving Eve
bruins.summary: NESN's Garden Party broadcast for Wednesday's game against Winnipeg starts at 6 p.m., with Andrew Raycroft joining Judd Sirott and Andy Brickley in the booth.

bruins.headline: Tuesday's practice lines
bruins.summary: Geekie–Lindholm–Pastrnak, Mittelstadt–Zacha–Peterka, Khusnutdinov–Minten–Poitras and Jeannot–Kuraly–Kastelic, with Mikey Eyssimont extra. The pairs were Lindholm–McAvoy, Zadorov–Borgen and Lohrei–Clifton.

bruins.headline: Sturm doesn't like the long breaks
bruins.summary: Boston had three days off before Winnipeg, its third such gap. "I do believe, overall, us as a team, we play better when we play a lot of games in a short time," Sturm said.

bruins.headline: Homestand ends against three Canadian teams
bruins.summary: Boston closes its six-game homestand against Winnipeg on Wednesday, Toronto on Friday at 1 p.m. and Vancouver on Sunday at 5 p.m. The Bruins beat the Jets 4–3 in overtime on Oct. 2.

bruins.headline: Clifton settling in on the third pair
bruins.summary: Connor Clifton has played four straight games, staying on the third pair with Mason Lohrei, with one assist, eight shots, six blocks and 13 hits in about 16 minutes a night. The Bruins had a full-team practice Sunday; Marco Sturm said, "We didn't do any video today; we just had a good skate."

bruins.headline: McAvoy's Thanksgiving: 20 family members and pies
bruins.summary: Charlie McAvoy and his wife are hosting 20 family members for Thanksgiving and will deliver pies to St. Francis House and Pine Street Inn. In the same feature, Sturm said he was "almost in shock" when Don Sweeney called to offer him the job.

bruins.headline: Lindholm's first four-goal game
bruins.summary: Elias Lindholm scored four times against Washington, his first four-goal game and first hat trick as a Bruin. He is tied with David Pastrnak for the team lead with 11 goals.

bruins.headline: McAvoy passes 300 career assists
bruins.summary: Charlie McAvoy had three assists against Washington, bringing him to 301 for his career. Jeremy Swayman made 30 saves and picked up an assist.

bruins.headline: Swayman third in NHL.com's quarter-season goalie vote
bruins.summary: Jeremy Swayman finished third in NHL.com's staff vote with 35 points, behind Wallstedt (60) and Kochetkov (58). He is 10–5–1 with a 2.50 goals-against average, a .908 save percentage and one shutout.

patriots.headline: Maye out at least six weeks
patriots.summary: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Drake Maye is out at least six weeks with his fractured right fibula. A return this season has not been ruled out.

patriots.headline: Patriots not adding a quarterback
patriots.summary: No team claimed Daniel Jones, and Mike Vrabel said adding a quarterback isn't "something that's going to happen here in the next few days." New England has two healthy QBs and none on the practice squad, and wants the reps to develop rookie Behren Morton.

patriots.headline: Vera-Tucker could return
patriots.summary: Alijah Vera-Tucker may be designated to return from injured reserve; "I think AVT has a chance to be out there," Vrabel said. Romeo Doubs could return later in the week.

patriots.headline: Vrabel: 'Tommy's our starter'
patriots.summary: Asked about Jones, Mike Vrabel said "Tommy's our starter." Tommy DeVito went 12-of-24 for 81 yards with a touchdown and an interception in relief in Munich and is 3–5 in eight career starts.

patriots.headline: No fine for Hutchinson's hit on Maye
patriots.summary: The NFL did not fine Detroit's Aidan Hutchinson for the sack that injured Maye. "I don't think it was anything intentional," Vrabel said.

patriots.headline: DeVito to start; Morton the backup
patriots.summary: Tommy DeVito is set to start at the Chargers, with rookie Behren Morton as the No. 2 quarterback. DeVito went 12-of-24 for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception in relief against Detroit.

patriots.headline: A.J. Brown expected to miss multiple weeks
patriots.summary: A.J. Brown's hamstring injury from the Lions game is expected to sideline him multiple weeks, his third missed stretch this season after a high ankle sprain and a knee flare-up. He has 11 catches for 128 yards in four games.

patriots.headline: Doubs eligible to return after the bye
patriots.summary: Patriots.com's bye-week review notes Romeo Doubs (shoulder) becomes eligible to come off injured reserve. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu are also on IR; the line has used six different combinations.

patriots.headline: Cassel's advice for DeVito
patriots.summary: Matt Cassel, who went 11–5 after replacing an injured Tom Brady in 2008, told Tommy DeVito to trust offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels: "Josh will put you in a great position to be successful."

patriots.headline: Chargers game flexed out of Sunday night
patriots.summary: The NFL moved Patriots at Chargers on Nov. 29 from Sunday Night Football to 4:05 p.m. on CBS; Raiders at Browns takes the 8:20 p.m. slot. New England's Dec. 10 Thursday game against Minnesota and its Dec. 21 Monday game against Kansas City stay in prime time.

redsox.headline: Duran and Casas tendered
redsox.summary: Boston tendered all of its remaining arbitration-eligible players at the Nov. 20 deadline, including Jarren Duran (projected $11.1 million) and Triston Casas (projected $1.7 million). None has agreed to terms yet.

redsox.headline: Connor Wong non-tendered
redsox.summary: Catcher Connor Wong, designated for assignment after the Nick Fortes trade, was non-tendered and became a free agent.

redsox.headline: Oviedo traded to Arizona
redsox.summary: Boston traded right-hander Johan Oviedo to the Diamondbacks for minor league lefty Luke Dotson, 22, and a player to be named later or cash. Oviedo pitched once for Boston, on March 30, before going on the injured list with a right elbow strain.

redsox.headline: Gil signs with Detroit
redsox.summary: Luis Gil signed a one-year, $2.3 million deal with the Tigers, per ESPN's Jeff Passan. Boston had interest, per the Globe, but never made an offer, per MassLive.

redsox.headline: Four bench players avoid arbitration
redsox.summary: Gonzalez, Monasterio, White and Jones signed one-year deals on deadline day.

redsox.headline: Gray: a Red Sox reunion 'never really came up'
redsox.summary: Sonny Gray, who signed with Minnesota, said talks with Boston "never really got close" but that "Boston was great… I loved it there, man. I truly did."

redsox.headline: Fortes to back up Rutschman
redsox.summary: Nick Fortes, acquired from Tampa Bay for 17-year-old right-hander Angel Roa, hit .258 with 6 homers and 35 RBIs in 109 games in 2026. Craig Breslow called him a "really strong defender who has a great reputation in working with a pitching staff." Connor Wong was designated for assignment to make room.

redsox.headline: Breslow: 'I think we have a good lineup'
redsox.summary: With Jake Bauers signed for four years and $58 million, Craig Breslow said, "I think we have a good lineup," and that it's hard to envision something else significant on the horizon. Bauers had a .389 on-base percentage in 2026, third in the majors.

redsox.headline: Red Sox agree to four years with Jake Bauers
redsox.summary: Boston agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal with Jake Bauers, the NLCS MVP for the champion Brewers. He hit .266 with 26 homers and 86 RBIs in 2026, mostly at first base. Because he turned down a qualifying offer, the Red Sox give up two draft picks and $1 million in international bonus pool money.

redsox.headline: Breslow promoted to president of baseball operations
redsox.summary: The Red Sox gave Craig Breslow, entering his fourth season running the club, the title of president of baseball operations, last held by Dave Dombrowski. Breslow said it doesn't change his approach.

nba.cutNote: Top 6 make the playoffs, 7–10 the play-in

nhl.cutNote: Top 3 in each division plus 2 wild cards make the playoffs

nfl.cutNote: Top 7 make the playoffs (division winners seeded 1–4)
